Method of Attack: Malware embedded in CCleaner application versions offered between August 15 and September 12
First-stage malware executed on 32-bit platforms only, collected data about infected PCs and sent to remote C&C server
Second-stage payload was a stealthy backdoor trojan sent based on filters run on infected hosts
Attackers used a MariaDB database on the C&C server to store infection data and determine targets
Attackers targeted large technology firms' networks for second-stage backdoor installation
Impacted Systems: 32-bit platforms running CCleaner versions from August 15 to September 12
Networks of large technology firms including Google, Microsoft, HTC, Samsung, Intel, Sony, VMWare, O2, Vodafone, Linksys, Epson, MSI, Akamai, DLink, Oracle (Dyn), Gauselmann, Singtel
Date of Discovery: September 18, 2017 (Monday when incident came to light)
Attack Vector: Malicious CCleaner application binaries downloaded by users
Data exfiltration via first-stage malware to remote C&C server
Second-stage backdoor trojan deployed selectively based on C&C server filters
Indicators of Compromise: Tainted CCleaner executables detected by security firms
C&C server logs showing infection data between September 12 and September 16
Database wiped on September 12 due to disk space exhaustion
700,000 entries for first-stage infections and 20 entries for second-stage infections in database before wipe
